Formication is not seen in a relapse of anxiety states. Delirium may be a feature of benzodiazepine withdrawal if high doses are rapidly
withdrawn; it is not a common feature.

questions.question_text: During alcohol withdrawal, generalized seizures usually occur within how many hours after the cessation of drinking?
questions.explanation:
During alcohol withdrawal, generalised seizures usually occur within 24 hours of cessation but occur later in some cases. These are grand-
mal seizures especially common in those who had previous seizures (epilepsy or withdrawal seizures), head injury and electrolyte imbalance
such as hyponatraemia or hypokalemia.

questions.question_text: Regarding the length of community detoxi�cation for opioid dependence, methadone reductions are typically carried out over a period of
questions.explanation:
Regarding the length of community detoxi�cation for opioid dependence, NICE guidelines state 'dose reduction can take place over anything
from a few days to several months, with a higher initial stabilisation dose taking longer to taper'and indicate that 'up to 3 months is typical
for methadone reduction, while Buprenorphine reductions are typically carried out over 14 days to a few weeks. In practice, detoxi�cation in
the community may extend over a longer period, if this facilitates the patient's comfort during the process. Ref: NICE; Drug misuse, opioid
detoxi�cation, clinical guidance 52,2007

questions.question_text: Which is the best known and the most widespread of the voluntary self-help organisations for problem drinkers?
questions.explanation:
Alcoholics Anonymous (AA) is the most established of the voluntary self-help organizations for problem drinkers. Bill Wilson and Dr Bob
Smith, both problem drinkers, found the AA in 1935 in the USA. Currently, there are ~3000 groups in the UK and ~88 000 groups worldwide.
Associated organisations are Al-anon (for relatives of problem drinkers); Al-Ateen (for teenage children of problem drinkers) Narcotics
Anonymous (NA) (for addicts of illicit drugs). Ref: Oxford handbook of psychiatry; 521

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a negative prognostic factor in patients with a history of alcohol dependence?
questions.explanation:
Positive factors: Being motivated to change; supportive family or relationship; in employment; treatable comorbid illness (e.g. anxiety
disorder, social phobia); accepting of appropriate treatment goal; AA involvement. Negative factors- Ambivalent to change; unstable
accommodation or homeless; drinking embedded into lifestyle (e.g. limited pursuits outside alcohol, all friends are drinkers); repeated
treatment failures; cognitive impairment. Ref: Oxford Handbook of Psychiatry; 515

questions.question_text: In PTSD which of the following statement is true?

options.text: Refugees are at no more risk than the indigenous population
Misdiagnosis as refractory depression does not occur
Securely attached individuals exhibit more symptoms.

questions.explanation:
Cortisol levels are low in PTSD. Insecure attachment increases risk of PTSD. PTSD is often misdiagnosed as depression. Refugees have higher
risk of PTSD. Avoidance of traumatic stimuli is associated with chronicity.

questions.question_text: In traumatic brain injury, the best predictor of outcome is the period of
questions.explanation:
After head injury, patients who are not able to resume previous activities are the ones who had a longer duration of PTA than those who
resumed work without problems.

questions.question_text: Intermittent dosing using SSRIs is e�ective in treatment of;
questions.explanation:
PMS: Intermittent dosing during the luteal phase of the menstrual cycle is e�ective. This temporarily increases serotonin concentration
during the luteal phase. Intermittent dosing is e�ective only in luteal phase, 2 weeks prior to menses. Most e�ective- Fluoxetine. E�ective
within one menstrual cycle - too rapid for antidepressant e�ect. Insomnia, GIT disturbances and fatigue are most common side e�ect. There
was no signi�cant di�erence in symptom reduction between continuous and intermittent dosing.

questions.question_text:
Lucy and Linda are twin sisters; Lucy has type 1 bipolar while Linda has type 2. Which of the following statements regarding their illnesses is
correct?

options.text: Lucy's diagnosis is more likely to change than Linda's diagnosis
Lucy is more likely to commit suicide than Linda
All of the other listed options are incorrect.
Lucy will spend more time in depression than Linda
Linda will have better functional recovery than Lucy

correct_answer.text: All of the other listed options are incorrect.

questions.explanation:
Bipolar II disorder is often thought of as a milder expression of bipolar disorder. However, it is only milder in its severity of manic symptoms
as hypomania is less severe than mania. Patients with bipolar type II disorder su�er more depressed days than patients with bipolar type I
disorder over time. According to prospective studies, bipolar II patients experienced mood symptoms 54% of the time compared with 47% in
bipolar I patients. For both bipolar I and bipolar II patients, those mood symptoms were dominated by depressive versus manic symptoms,
although bipolar II patients experienced more depressive symptoms (93%) than bipolar I patients (67%). This �nding may explain the
increased suicidality rates and poor functional recovery observed among bipolar 2 patients (Keck, 2007).

questions.question_text: Male to female ratio of somatisation disorder is
questions.explanation:
Somatisation is twice as common in women as in men. Shorter Oxford Textbook Page 208. Please note that this ratio is derived from cross-
sectional prevalence of somatisation. The WHO collaborative study of psychological problems in general health care identi�ed a major
conceptual problem in measuring somatoform disorders in community - the stability of such diagnosis was very poor irrespective of
'lifetime' de�nitions of syndromes such as somatisation disorder. Though cross sectionally the number of patients meeting the criteria at a
given time remained stable, only 25% of the same patients meeting criteria for somatoform disorders at baseline also met these criteria 1
year later. Nearly 61% of lifetime symptoms reported at baseline were not reported at follow-up. This marked discrepancy was attributed to
inconsistent recall, implicating that cross-sectional surveys of somatoform disorders are highly unreliable. Simon G, Gureje O: Stability of
somatization disorder and somatization symptoms among primary care patients. Arch Gen Psychiatry 1999; 56:90-95

questions.question_text:
Mr P is a 28-year-old gentleman who has su�ered 2 episodes of mania and 2 episodes of depression over the last 6 years. What is the most
likely estimate of the mean age of onset of his illness?
questions.explanation:
This patient has a diagnosis of Bipolar A�ective disorder. According to the Epidemiological Catchment Area (ECA) study the mean age of
onset of Bipolar is 21 and that of unipolar depression is 27. There is a female predominance of approximately 2:1 for unipolar disorder but
equal sex incidence is reported in bipolar disorder.

Tricyclic Antidepressant: They do not cause any signi�cant malformation in all three trimesters. But preferably use nortriptyline and
desipramine as they have less hypotensive and anticholinergic side e�ects. However, high dosages use (similar to �uoxetine) in third
trimester can lead reversible withdrawal symptoms (irritability, eating and sleeping di�culties and convulsions). Nortriptyline, amitriptyline,
impramine and �uoxetine are recommended antidepressants. Avoid paroxetine

questions.question_text:
One of your well educated patients �nds a large trial on antidepressants conducted in USA. He asks you a �urry of questions about this trial
called STAR*D. Which of the following is NOT true with respect to this trial?

options.text: Nearly one third of those who have depression do not respond to any of the four interventions
With each level of treatment proportion of responders increased
Switching to one antidepressant is not di�erent from another after a failed monotherapy.
It involved sequenced stepwise treatment for depression

correct_answer.text: With each level of treatment proportion of responders increased

questions.explanation:
STAR*D stands for Sequenced treatment alternative for depression. The study involved 4 possible 'steps' for treatment, and any patient who
failed to meet remission criteria at each step was then asked to move to the next level. Remission rates dropped while relapse rates
increased with moving higher to each level

questions.question_text: Postnatal depression usually lasts for less than
questions.explanation:
Postnatal depression (PND): A signi�cant depressive episode, temporally related to childbirth, occurring in 10-15% of women within 6
months post-partum (peak 3- 4 weeks). The clinical features are similar to other depressive episodes, although thought content may include
worries about the baby's health or the mother's ability to cope adequately with the baby. 90% of cases last less than 1 month; 4% greater
than one year. Ref: Oxford Handbook of Psychiatry: 2nd edn., Pg. 756

questions.question_text: Psychomotor disturbance is a key symptom in;
questions.explanation:
Catatonic schizophrenia is characterised by marked disturbance in motor behaviours, in addition to the general features of schizophrenia.
(Cata: Disturbed, Tonic: Tone). It can present in 3 forms; Excited catatonia, stuporus catatonia, catatonia alternating between excitement and
stupor.

questions.question_text: Regarding clinical features of hypomania and mania which of the following is correct?

options.text: Dysphoric hypomania is commonly seen in bipolar disorder
Hypomania can be regarded as a normal psychological state
Most hypomanic episodes in bipolar II disorder last for 4 days or longer.
Manic episodes can be associated with normal levels of social and occupational functioning
Duration is the most important criteria of di�erentiation

correct_answer.text: Dysphoric hypomania is commonly seen in bipolar disorder

questions.explanation:
The di�erentiation is mostly based on degree of functional impairment e.g. requirement for hospitalisation etc. Duration criteria is arbitrary (
4 days hypomania; 7 days mania) Hypomania is pathological not normal state. Dysphoric features and sometimes frank depression
(microepisodes) are common in hypomania or mania.

questions.question_text: Regarding epilepsy and its treatment all are true except

options.text: TCAs are the �rst line of treatment for depression in epilepsy
Visual hallucinations are common in ictal psychosis
Depression is common in patients with epilepsy
All anti-epileptics have been associated with psychiatric side e�ects

correct_answer.text: TCAs are the �rst line of treatment for depression in epilepsy

questions.explanation:
When antidepressants are necessary to treat depression in patients with epilepsy, selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs) and
multireceptor antidepressants are considered �rst-line treatments. Electroconvulsive therapy is not contraindicated for treatment-resistant
or psychotic depression.

questions.question_text:
Mr. Y su�ers from lung cancer and severe depression, which requires treatment with antidepressant medications. He has been complaining
of severe nausea and vomiting, as a result of taking chemotherapeutic agents. Which one among the following medications would be the
best choice for treatment of his depression?
questions.explanation:
Nausea is not a signi�cant side e�ect of mirtazapine due to its 5-HT3 antagonistic properties and could be used for patients taking
anticancer drugs, which has high propensity to induce nausea and vomiting. All the other drugs listed above have been shown to cause
considerably more nausea than placebo in clinical trails. Ref: Nutt D; mirtazapine; Pharmacology in relation to adverse events, Acta
Psychiatry Scand 1997; pg 31-37

questions.question_text: Research and investigations into sleep disorders have suggested that

options.text: There is a well known HLA polymorphism associated with REM sleep behaviour disorder
REM sleep behaviour disorder can precede future movement disorders.
Clonazepam is the �rst-line treatment for narcolepsy
Sleep latency of more than 10 min on overnight polysomnography is characteristic of narcolepsy

correct_answer.text: REM sleep behaviour disorder can precede future movement disorders.

questions.explanation:
REM sleep behavior disorder may actually precede the motor symptoms of Parkinson disease and as many as 20% of patents with REM
sleep behavior disorder eventually develop Parkinson disease.

questions.question_text: Risk factors for PTSD include which one of the following?
questions.explanation:
Lack of internal locus of control is a contributor to the development of PTSD. Being female, high degree of neuroticism and low sense of
security also increase the risk of PTSD after a trauma. Religious a�liation is seen as protective in various studies. Most studies showed a
positive relationship between PTSD and smoking and nicotine dependence, with odds ratios ranging between 2.04 and 4.52. Speci�c PTSD
symptoms may contribute to smoking and disrupt cessation attempts. But there is no evidence that smoking itself elevates the risk of PTSD
after exposure to trauma.  Nicotine Tob Res (2007) 9 (11): 1071-1084.

questions.question_text: Risk factors speci�c for bulimia rather than anorexia include
questions.explanation:
Risk factors for bulimia include (Fairburn and ; Harrison, 2003) female sex, adolescence and early adulthood, Western cultural adaptation,
family history of substance misuse, especially alcoholism or obesity, and a history of early menarche and peronal history of being
overweight.

questions.question_text: The association between cannabis and schizophrenia is characterised by all of the following except

options.text: Causality is confounded by amphetamine use

questions.explanation:
Cannabis has been strongly debated in the aetiology of schizophrenia. The pooled estimate for development of psychosis associated with
prior cannabis use is an odds ratio (OR) of 2.1 (95% CI: 1.7 to 2.5). This shows that the association between cannabis and later psychosis
outcome is consistent. Confounders such as amphetamine use are not able to explain the association by themselves. Reverse causality
remains plausible but cannot be proven i.e. patients do not smoke cannabis because they have psychotic mental state or distressed. In
Dunedin cohort, exposure at age 15 was measured against developing psychosis at age 26 and an association was present even after
adjusting for psychotic liability at age 11. A Greek cohort study examined the self-medication hypothesis by testing whether subtle psychotic
experiences with distress would have stronger associations with cannabis use than psychotic experiences without distress. But stronger
associations were found between cannabis and psychotic experiences in the absence of distress, making self-medication unlikely.
Nevertheless there are studies that suggest bidirectional association. Cannabis shows dose-response relationships to psychosis outcome;
exposure often precedes the outcome, and there is a plausible biological mechanism linking the cannabis and schizophrenia either via role
of endocannabinoids in neurodevelopment or dopamine sensitisation. Caspi et al, using Dunedin New Zealand birth cohort showed that a
functional polymorphism in the catechol-O-methyltransferase (COMT) gene moderates the e�ect of adolescent cannabis use on risk for
adult psychosis.

questions.question_text: The babies of anorexic mothers
questions.explanation:
Starvation and anorexia a�ects pregnancy adversely. Children born to anorexic mothers have low birth weight, microcephaly, and low
APGAR scores. In actively anorexic mother, the neonate may have hypoglycaemia.

questions.question_text: The delusions in persistent delusional disorders are usually
questions.explanation:
Delusional disorder is an uncommon condition in which patients present with circumscribed symptoms of non-bizarre delusions, but with
absence of prominent hallucinations and no thought disorder, mood disorder or signi�cant �attening of a�ect. Note that this distinction
between bizarre and non-bizarre content of delusions has been removed from DSM-5.

questions.question_text: The most common neuropsychiatric disorder associated with epilepsy is
questions.explanation:
Depression is seen in 30-50% of cases with epilepsy. There is possible relationship with lesion location eg in temporal lobe epilepsy. There is
also increased mortality secondary to suicide. Suicide risk is also increased x25 over non-epileptics. There is an increased prevalence of
conversion disorder in epileptics, including an increased risk of pseudoseizures. Cognitive deterioration is another important outcome of
chronic epilepsy and is caused by a number of factors including repeated seizures with cerebral hypoxia as well as the neurological e�ects of
chronic anti-convulsant therapy. The association between right-side TLE and manic illness was also described by Flor-Henry.

questions.question_text: The prevalence of psychiatric symptoms at the �rst presentation of Huntington's disease is
questions.explanation:
The Prevalence of psychiatric symptoms at the �rst presentation of Huntington's disease is 30%. Suicide rates 4 times higher than general
population (note una�ected family members also have higher suicide risk, sometimes as high as patients). 3-6% of cases a schizophreniform
psychosis is the �rst presentation of Huntington's disease. OCD like symptoms may occur due to basal ganglia involvement. MRI shows
caudate atrophy (head) and resultant box-car ventricles.

questions.question_text: The prevalence of somatoform pain disorder is;
questions.explanation:
A study in Belgium reported that somatization syndrome is the third highest psychiatric disorder, with a prevalence rate of 8.9%. The �rst
and second most common psychiatric disorders were depression and anxiety disorders.

questions.question_text: The risk of neonatal withdrawal symptoms is high with which of the following antidepressants?
questions.explanation: Risk of neonatal withdrawal symptoms is high with Paroxetine and Venlafaxine due to short half life

questions.question_text: The SF-36 scale measures which of the following?
questions.explanation:
Health-related quality of life (HRQOL) refers to functioning and well-being in physical, mental and social dimensions of life. The SF-36 is a
frequently used multi-item HRQOL instrument. The SF-36 Health Survey (36 item short form health survey) is a generic outcome measure
designed to examine a person's perceived health status. Outcome studies using the SF-36 can be done at outpatient clinics, via postal survey
or telephone interview. The SF-36 can also be used in a computerised format. It assesses physical, social and mental well-being.

questions.question_text: The suicide rates vary between European countries by a factor of about;
questions.explanation:
Suicide rates in Europe vary widely with countries such as Spain, Italy and Greece reporting rates below 7 per 100000 inhabitants, whereas
others such as Hungary and Finland report rates in excess of 72 per 100000 inhabitants.

questions.question_text: The use of SSRIs in pregnancy is associated with no general increase in the rates of major malformations with the exception of
questions.explanation:
SSRI: No increase in major malformation (exception- paroxetine); the neonatal withdrawal are reversible complications. However there is
13.3% increase in spontaneous abortion (also with mirtazepine and bupropion), decreased gestational age (mean 1 week) and low birth
weight (mean 175 gms). Paroxetine, particularly high dose �rst trimesters exposure, is clearly linked to cardiac malformation - VSD and ASD.
Third trimester use can give rise to neonatal complication due to abrupt withdrawals.

questions.question_text: Vulnerability factors for PTSD include
questions.explanation:
Factors associated with post-traumatic stress disorder (from Bisson, 2007) include pretraumatic factors such as previous psychiatric
disorders including personality dysfunction, female gender, an external locus of control greater than internal locus of control, lower
socioeconomic status and past history of childhood unresolved trauma among others. High IQ, high social class and male gender may be
protective.

questions.question_text: What is the most characteristic symptom of a patient with SSRI discontinuation syndrome?
questions.explanation:
The abrupt withdrawal of SSRI especially paroxetine or �uvoxamine (shorter half-life), is associated with dizziness, nausea, headache,
depression, anxiety, insomnia, poor concentration, �u-like symptoms, paresthesias, and migraine-like symptoms. It usually requires at least
6 weeks of treatment before discontinuation and resolves spontaneously in 3 weeks. Those who have signi�cant SSRI intolerance during
treatment onset will have more discontinuation reactions.

questions.question_text: What is the most vulnerable period for teratogenic e�ects during pregnancy?
questions.explanation:
Teratogenic e�ects are both dose and time dependent, with organs at the greatest risk during their period of fastest development. Week 6
to week 10 is the most vulnerable period.

questions.question_text: What is the percentage of patients with schizophrenia that discontinue antipsychotics within 18 months of treatment?
questions.explanation: According to CATIE trial data 70 to 75% of patients who are prescribed antipsychotics will discontinue them in 18 months.

questions.question_text: When co-prescribed with lithium, which drug can increase the likelihood of neurotoxicity of lithium?
questions.explanation:
Although haloperidol and lithium have been used safely together in many patients, there have been some reported cases of
encephalopathic syndrome consisting of severe neurotoxic e�ects and extrapyramidal symptoms, followed by irreversible brain damage,
associated with the combination. The mechanism is unknown. Drugs such as loop diuretics, thiazides, NSAIDs, ACE-Inhibitors, �uoxetine
could raise lithium levels and increase the likelihood of neurotoxicity.

questions.question_text: Which of the following factors are generally accepted as predictors of unfavourable outcome in schizophrenia?

options.text: Short duration and presence of precipitating stressor
Acute onset and predominantly positive symptoms
Female sex, older age of onset and married status
Previous psychiatric illness and a poor educational record
Higher social economical status and living in a developing country

correct_answer.text: Previous psychiatric illness and a poor educational record

questions.explanation:
The poor prognostic factors in schizophrenia include early onset (less than 20 years of age), insidious onset, male sex, poor social support,
or unmarried status, absence of stressor, chronic course more than 2 years, poor pre-morbid adjustment, predominance of negative
symptoms, past history of schizophrenia, family history of schizophrenia, �at or blunted a�ect and poor response to treatment.

questions.question_text: Which among the following has the best evidence-based non-pharmacological treatment for insomnia?
questions.explanation:
Stimulus control therapy. Sleep problems are often triggered by stressful or disturbinglife events, such as serious illness, hospitalization or
death of a loved one. Once the situation has been resolved, sleep usually returns to normal. However, sometimes the insomnia can remain.
This is because a negative association between going to bed and not sleeping has been formed. These negative emotions automatically
triggered by going to bed increase alertness and make it more di�cult to get to sleep. This type of insomnia is often referred to as
conditioned insomnia. Stimulus control therapy replaces these learned negative responses with positive ones. It makes the bed and
bedroom positive triggers for sleep, ensuring that when the patient goes to bed or wakes up during the night, they can expect to fall asleep
easily. Most patients need about three to four weeks of treatment to undo the maladaptive learning of conditioned insomnia. Ref: Non-
pharmacological treatment options by William Dollman

questions.question_text: Which of the following criteria must be met before clozapine is prescribed according to its licensing indications in the UK?

options.text: 2 antipsychotics tried for a total duration of 2 months
1 typical and 1 atypical tried sequentially for a total duration of 1 month
1 atypical and 1 typical tried in combination for more than 2 months
1 atypical and 1 typical tried sequentially for a total duration of 2 months

correct_answer.text: 1 atypical and 1 typical tried sequentially for a total duration of 2 months

questions.explanation:
Under the terms of its UK license clozapine should only be used for patients with schizophrenia who are unresponsive to two or more anti-
psychotics (at least one must be atypical) or who are intolerant of their neurological side e�ects.

questions.question_text:
A 46-year-old woman has a history of recurrent depressive episodes each followed by brief hypomania. She recovers from the most recent
episode. Which of the following prophylactic treatments would you recommend for this woman?
questions.explanation:
Lithium monotherapy is the �rst line. It is probably e�ective against both manic and depressive relapse, although it is more e�ective in
preventing mania. Lithium is also associated with a reduced risk of suicide in bipolar disorder

questions.question_text:
A 36-year-old woman with a history of bipolar disorder has developed symptoms of hypomania. She has a 3-month-old baby and is
breastfeeding her. She is currently not on any medications and wishes to continue breastfeeding. Which one of the following is the safest to
allow her to continue breastfeeding?
questions.explanation:
Sodium valproate has been recommended to be used in breast-feeding mothers. The manufacturers of sodium valproate state that there
appears to be no contraindication to its use in breast-feeding.

questions.question_text:
Which of the following group of medications is associated with an elevated risk of persistent pulmonary hypertension in infants when
exposed during pregnancy?
questions.explanation: SSRI use during late pregnancy is related to an increased risk of persistent pulmonary hypertension in the newborn (Chambers 2006).

questions.question_text: A girl was sexually abused by her father, who denies responsibility. Regarding support for her un-abused siblings, which approach is best?

options.text: Family therapy with an appropriate therapist including the abuser
Family therapy with an appropriate therapist excluding the abuser

questions.explanation:
Each sibling would be given the opportunity to explore what issues may be present in an individual and con�dential setting, and some
information may not be necessary or appropriately shared with all siblings. Child psychotherapy may not be suitable for siblings who are
older and for whom this therapy would not be suitable.

questions.question_text: Role transitions are a major focus of therapy in which of the following models?
questions.explanation:
Managing role transitions characterised by a change from one role to other - e.g. graduation, beginning or end of career, migration, medical
ill health, etc. is one of the cornerstones of IPT

questions.question_text: Which of the following investigatory �ndings is most supportive of a diagnosis of Huntington's disease?

options.text: HMPAO-SPECT scan shows patchy hypo perfusion throughout the brain
EEG shows spike and wave activity
MRI scan shows atrophy of head of the caudate nucleus
Raised white cell count on lumbar puncture

questions.question_text:
Mr. Y has been assessed in the memory clinic and diagnosed with Alzheimer's disease of moderate severity. He has been started on
Rivastigmine. His wife wants to know the most common side e�ect of this medication. The correct answer is;
questions.explanation: The common side e�ects of rivastigmine include nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, dizziness and anorexia.

questions.question_text: Which personality disorder is mostly associated with suicide in patients over the age of 60?
questions.explanation:
Harwood and colleagues compared suicides, and natural death controls age 60 years and over on ICD-10 "personality trait accentuation"
(Harwood et al. 2001). Anankastic (obsessional) and anxious traits, signi�cantly distinguished the groups. These traits are also strongly

questions.question_text:
An 83-year-old gentleman with Alzheimers dementia has also developed some psychotic symptoms and was due to be started on an
antipsychotic medication. Which one of the following would lead to an increase in the risk of stroke?
questions.explanation:
Having reviewed the literature on the use of Olanzapine and Risperidone for the behavioural and psychological symptoms of dementia, the
committee on safety of medicines concluded that each was associated with at least two-fold increase in the risk of stroke and should,
therefore, be no longer used in dementia (Du� 2004)

questions.question_text: Which of the following is contraindicated in the elderly with psychosis and cognitive impairment?
questions.explanation:
Antipsychotics have been the most commonly used treatment for psychotic symptoms. Their usefulness in treating schizophrenia (both late
onset and very late onset psychosis) in elderly people is well established. The atypical antipsychotics, which have a better side-e�ect pro�le,
are considered to be more suitable for elderly people. But more recently there have been concerns raised regarding their safety in psychosis
due to dementia. The Committee on Safety of Medicine concluded that Olanzapine and Risperidone was associated with a two-fold increase
in the risk of stroke (a small but signi�cant risk of cerebrovascular events) in elderly patients especially in people over age 80. In elderly
people, age-related bodily changes a�ect the pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics of antipsychotic drugs, which have numerous side
e�ects that can be more persistent and disabled in older people (Ref:

questions.question_text:
A pregnant woman has a �ve-year-old son who has been observed with childhood autism. She is keen to know how likely it is for her unborn
child also to have the same condition.
questions.explanation:
The recurrence rate in siblings of a�ected children is 2% to 8%, much higher than the prevalence rate in the general population but much
lower than in single-gene diseases. This translates to 50 times (range: 30 - 120) relative risk in siblings. The risk of autistic disorder in a sibling
of 2 autistic children: 25-30% (nearly 300 times higher) [Excerpt retrieved from Muhle R, Trentacoste SV, Rapin I. The genetics of autism.
Pediatrics 2004; 113(5):472-486].

questions.question_text: Which of the following suggests a subcultural rather than a biological cause for learning disability?

options.text: Equal distribution across families of di�erent types of socio-economic status
Moderate/ severe impairment in intellectual abilities
Men are more commonly a�ected than females
Intellectual ability is impaired in family members

correct_answer.text: Intellectual ability is impaired in family members

questions.explanation:
In subcultural LD, family members may also have borderline IQ. Their intellectual disability is usually mild or borderline type. It is more
common in lower socioeconomic groups. Dysmorphic features are less likely. Syndromic features are not seen. Behavioural phenotypes are
rare.

questions.question_text:
An 18-year-old man shows repeated episodes of violent behaviour causing bodily injury and property damage. Police have been called on
numerous occasions. There is a restraining order against him. He does not show any other problems with his behaviour or conduct and
feels remorseful for his behaviour. The most appropriate treatment is
questions.explanation:
Intermittent explosive disorder is classi�ed as an impulse control disorder in DSM 5. DSM 5 recognises 2 variants: high frequency/low-

guilt and remorse. Patients do not show any other conduct problems generally. Treatment is empirical, and some evidence exists for the use
of mood stabilizers especially carbamazepine, lithium and valproate.

questions.question_text: The most common psychiatric problem associated with homicides is
questions.explanation:
A minority of homicide o�enders are mentally disordered. Alcohol and drug dependence most common, then personality disorder.
Schizophrenia, delusional disorder, and depression may be relevant in a few cases. Ref: Kaplan and Sadock Synopsis of Psychiatry 9th
edition; Pg 1352.

questions.question_text: The percentage of domestic violence incidents reported to general practitioners is
questions.explanation:
Sadly many incidents of domestic violence are unreported, not recorded or not prosecuted; therefore domestic violence is often described
as a 'hidden crime'. After police, medical sta� were the next most likely to hear of incidents (they were told about 10% of all incidents), and
were more likely to o�er advice and support than the police (they did so in 70% of incidents they were told about). British Crime Survey 1996

questions.question_text: Which of the following is classi�ed under 'crimes of dishonesty'?
questions.explanation:
Crimes against the person include o�ences of interpersonal violence (minor assault, homicide), sexual o�ences (indecent exposure, rape)
and robbery. Crimes of dishonesty include burglary; theft and handling stolen goods; fraud and forgery. Property damage and arson are

questions.question_text: The most common psychiatric disorder seen as a comorbidity of autism in children is
questions.explanation:
Depression is quoted as the most common comorbidity in adults with ASD. If learning disability is considered as a comorbidity, then it will be
the most common comorbidity. Seventy percent of participants had at least one comorbid disorder, and 41% had two or more. The most

(28.2%, 95% CI 13.3-43.0), and oppositional de�ant disorder (28.1%, 95% CI 13.9-42.2). Of those with attention-de�cit/hyperactivity disorder,
84% received a second comorbid diagnosis. Simono� E et al. Psychiatric disorders in children with autism spectrum disorders: prevalence,
comorbidity, and associated factors in a population derived sample. J Am Acad Child Adolesc Psychiatry. 2008 Aug;47(8):921-9.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following is a technique used in CBT?
questions.explanation:
In CBT, the purpose of Socratic questioning by the therapist is to prompt the patient to examine the accuracy of maladaptive thoughts that
are causing psychological distress. It does require therapists to be highly active in asking challenging questions of the patient when they
identify maladaptive thoughts.
